I've left comments inline about some of the community guidelines for  new APIs in libpldm.
 As this is failing CI, I expect this is still WIP. I will review it again more thoughtfully when it's done.
Hi Aditya, thanks for the change. I have a few comments inline.
Doxygen format
Done

I recognise that historically the structs have been packed, but that's no longer desirable.

See: https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md?plain=1#L298-L299
Done, the struct is no longer packed.

Please avoid decomposing the message members into function parameters.

See: https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md?plain=1#L287-L293
Done. Using a struct instead of decomposing function params.

Following the guidelines [https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blame/06dcea74c3f956956b9c345c255069054ef66f1c/CONTRIBUTING.md#L287], this should accept a struct instead of decomposing the input parameters.
Also, I'm missing the corresponding decode_set_numeric_effecter_enable_req?
Done. Using a struct instead of decomposing function params.
Currently we don't have use case for this. But I will try to implement and add it.

I understand that there is currently no use case for this within pldmd, but we should aim to make the library usable both for pldmd (inside the BMC) and for any PLDM device implementation that chooses to use our library. Of course, this means the decode function will remain marked as LIBPLDM_ABI_TESTING, since an example usage will not be made public.

In fact, this is one of the requirements for adding a new API, as described in the contributing guidelines:
https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/06dcea74c3f956956b9c345c255069054ef66f1c/CONTRIBUTING.md?plain=1#L268
I Agree. I will implement it.
Done
Writing `// NOLINTNEXTLINE (...)` should be a hint that what you're doing is not desirable. See @roger.gili-coscojuela@sipearl.com's comment below.
Done. Replaced with placement new.

The community is pivoting over using the placement new instead of the reinterpret_cast. See other example usages in the file, for example here:
https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/06dcea74c3f956956b9c345c255069054ef66f1c/tests/dsp/platform.cpp#L785

same for all other occurrences in the patch.
Done. Replaced with placement new.
@andrew@codeconstruct.com.au @roger.gili-coscojuela@sipearl.com apologies for the late reply. I have addressed your comments.
This documentation should instead be on the struct.
Done

Perhaps I should have mentioned in the previous comment, but you should take advantage of `PLDM_MSG_DEFINE_P()` here:

https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/06dcea74c3f956956b9c345c255069054ef66f1c/include/libpldm/base.h#L246-L260

Please fix throughout
Done

Please don't do this. In general you have no guarantee that the encoded message layout matches the layout of the C struct. Instead, provide a manually encoded `std::array<uint8_t>` or `std::vector<uint8_t>` and compare the encoded payload bytes to the expected bytes. You may do _that_ via `memcmp()` if you like, but what you have here is not generally correct or maintainable.

Please fix throughout
Done
Please ensure your Author, Commit and Signed-off-by values are consistent.
Done

v1.2.0 was released on 1 Nov 2019. The latest revision, v1.3.0 was released 5 Aug 2024. We can't do better than that, and it's still over a year old. But that's a much better place than referencing a 6-year-old version.

Can you please use the most recent specification (currently v1.3.0) as a reference?
Done
Hi Aditya, thanks for the patch. I have some requests inline.
Nit: Adding version may be not needed in this case, Latest (v1.3.0) also same struct. For nor make it generic.
Done

I'd rather we try to keep this succinct and just reference the function, so:

```suggestion
- platform: Added `encode_set_numeric_effecter_enable_req()`
```
Done

I've left some comments regarding symbol prefixes below. I'd like to start fixing these defines as well, so:

```suggestion
#define PLDM_PLATFORM_SET_NUMERIC_EFFECTER_ENABLE_REQ_BYTES 3
```
Done

Please prefix the symbol with the specification identifier:

https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/bf554b2a15505052e7f6803f8ff728465193a0b6/CONTRIBUTING.md#L260-L262

So in this case, `struct pldm_platform_set_numeric_effecter_enable_req`.

I recognise this is inconsistent with e.g `struct pldm_set_numeric_sensor_enable_req`, but I'd rather we have consistent rules going forward rather than bind ourselves to problems of the past.
Done
Please ensure you update the type name here.
Done
`payload_length` should be an `[in,out]` parameter so the caller can learn the length used in the payload buffer.
Done
Please document these in the same order as they're declared in the function prototype.
Done

Similar prefixing here too please:

```
int encode_pldm_platform_set_numeric_effecter_enable_req(...)
```
Done
Needs to be `size_t *payload_length`.
Done

Using `pldm_msgbuf_complete_consumed()` constrains the caller to providing an exactly-sized buffer. Instead, for `encode_*()` APIs, please prefer using `pldm_msgbuf_complete_used(buf, *payload_length, payload_length)` so the caller can learn the length consumed in the payload buffer.
Done

Must be `ASSERT_EQ(...)` to prevent undefined behaviour due to uninitialised memory in the `memcmp()` below.

Please fix throughout.
Done
I have addressed all the changes. The patch: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/libpldm/+/85429/8 was squashed with this one.
